name: rain_torus_w0

geometry.kind: sink (2) where x % 3 == 1 and y % 3 == 1, source (1) elsewhere

stimulus.click: a click is a rain at the nearest source cell (mu_rain for rain_dur ticks)

niche_choice: Numbers fixed before any organism lives here, by one principle: separated timescales, rain (50 ticks) << food lifetime after rain (~10^2-10^3 ticks) << richness drift (2000 ticks, as W2). Rich and lean times vary at random (user's choice, 2026-10-26). Never tuned on an organism's result.
notes: Everything the world does is a rule of the Lean table: rain, drying and waste removal are exchanges with the outer reservoir at the stimulus potential (supply rule), spreading is the diffusion rule; the simulator computes their rates from the same formulas (gate check nested_world_rates_match_lean).
dissolution: physics (2026-10-27, after G26c and frees_only_by_dissolving): a body without intact membrane dissolves into the cell's waste pool with everything it holds (B plus inner content); conductance is symmetric Metropolis, kappa_dis * exp(-|dE|/2), so downhill dissolution runs at kappa_dis = 0.005 (a corpse lasts ~200 ticks) and the reverse (a dead body forming from waste) at kappa_dis * exp(-|dE|). B = 16; the reverse is negligible at the waste levels of this world (simulators omit it; the cross-check reports the bound).
food_energy: physics (2026-10-27): a food quantum carries chemical energy foodE = 8 relative to a waste quantum (food is free energy, not only matter; derived earlier for the 2D world, forgotten in the first nested table). The food reservoir potentials shift by +8 (dry 0, rain 16), so the world's own dynamics are unchanged; only the organism's food and waste exchanges see the difference. Without it food and waste were the same content at different concentrations and bodies condensed out of concentrated waste.
